transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-07 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood Solutions), Ruth (PixelWorkz VP Partnerships), Omar (CTO), Lena (Head of Cloud), Jae (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
PixelWorkz exploring partner onramp for GPU capacity and hybrid routing. Focus on dedicated capacity/reseller model, VPC private deployments, SOC2/compliance, and pilot sizing for image-gen inference workloads. Discussed latency/cost trade-offs, KV cache and batching benefits, and possible benchmarks. Next: deck, benchmark plan, schedule POC kick-off.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're super excited to talk through how Redwood can fit into PixelWorkz's GPU onramp. I'm Maya, AE on the partner team, uh Diego will jump into the technical parts.
[00:08] Ruth: Thanks Maya, hi team, we appreciate you. Quick intro, I'm Ruth, run partnerships here, and Omar's our CTO, Lena runs cloud infra.
[00:15] Omar: Heyeveryone, apologies for being slightly late, connection was finicky.
[00:20] Diego: No problem, welcome. Maybe quick round — what's top of mind for you folks in a partnership?
[00:28] Ruth: Two main things: one, we need a path to resell predictable GPU capacity to customers who want a managed option; two, we want a private/VPC offering for larger enterprise deals. Pricing and compliance are big fences.
[00:42] Maya: Totally. For the resale model we typically offer dedicated pools and marketplace onramps; for enterprise we do Redwood Private with a customer-controlled VPC and KMS/HSM support.
[00:52] Lena: When you say "Redwood Private" — is that something we host, or you host in our VPC? There's a couple of ways we could approach it.
[01:00] Diego: Good question. We do a few patterns: hosted control plane with a customer-managed VPC peering, or a fully on-prem bundle where control plane sits behind your network. Both support RBAC and audit logging.
[01:12] Jae: For the on-prem option what kind of footprint are we looking at? Our infra team runs Ampere A100-ish nodes and some Ada-gen instances on prem.
[01:22] Diego: Footprint depends on the workload. For image-gen workload you mentioned in the prep doc, you should expect: model variants (1-7B to 34B) map to different GPU counts; we can supply a recommended node sizing. Also important is sequence length profile — even for images the prompt tokens and conditioning matter for KV cache sizing.
[01:40] Omar: One thing I want to call out — our existing customers often ask for deterministic p95 latency under load. How does Redwood guarantee that with batching?
[01:50] Diego: We tune autoscaling and continuous batching by SLOs; our smart router can route low-latency traffic to dedicated low-batch lanes and bigger batch lanes for throughput. There's a tradeoff: you pay more for lower latency because you lose batching efficiency. We can show concrete numbers in the benchmark.
[02:08] Ruth: And on security — SOC2 is table stakes. We also need audit trails, SSO with SAML, and encryption keys in our KMS.
[02:16] Maya: We support SOC2, SAML SSO with IdP integrations, per-route audit logs, and customer KMS integrations — HSM via AWS KMS or GCP KMS, and we have an on-prem HSM option for Private. We'll share the security pack.
[02:29] Jae: Any gotchas with KV cache and stateful routing if we run across multiple datacenters? We can't have KV tied to a single rack if the customer spans regions.
[02:38] Diego: Good point — we have cross-region KV replication patterns and sticky routing, but cross-region will add latency for cache warmups. For most workloads we recommend regional caching with fallback cold path to nearest region.
[02:50] Omar: Pricing — do you do resale margins for partners or is it reseller BYO pricing?
[02:56] Maya: We have partner pricing tiers with committed capacity discounts; for resellers we can offer a markup-friendly billing contract or reseller margins on committed pallets. We'll share sample SOW/pricing.
[03:08] Ruth: Great. Also curious on telemetry — how deep does observability go? Our ops team expects token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
[03:18] Diego: Console has per-model/per-route latency and token cost breakdowns, tracing hooks, and request-level logs. For Private we'll mirror that but you can host metrics in your own monitoring with our tracing integrations.
[03:29] Samir: To be explicit, the pilot we usually recommend is a small dedicated pool for a single top customer or internal demo — run 2-4 GPUs initially with a surge policy, measure p50/p95 and cost-per-1k tokens.
[03:45] Ruth: Ok that aligns — our initial pilot likely targets 3 enterprise customers who need low-latency image inferencing.
[03:52] Diego: For the benchmark we should capture: steady-state QPS, burst QPS, p50/p95, token-cost, and cold-start characteristics for KV cache. I'll draft a test plan.
[04:05] Jae: We'll provide representative prompts, average token length, and current QPS data.
[04:10] Omar: Any limitations on model repo? We use a mix of open LLMs and a few custom finetuned weights — can we bring our own weights?
[04:18] Maya: Yes — we support customer-supplied models in Private and Dedicated contexts; there are licensing checks but technically supported. For hosted catalog we curate open models and Redwood-verified variants.
[04:30] Ruth: Oh, one more thing: we've been talking to Run:ai and Lambda Labs — can you summarize how Redwood differentiation looks from partner perspective?
[04:38] Diego: Sure — high level: we focus on production-grade inference controls (continuous batching, KV cache, smart routing), unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost-aware tuning with recommendations. Run:ai focuses on cluster orchestration, Lambda sells hardware plus managed services — our angle is runtime + ops + partner-friendly contract models.
[04:58] Ruth: Makes sense.
[05:02] Maya: Quick note — some transcription may spell things oddly, but we'll attach the slides.

[05:12] --- technical deep dive segment ---
[05:15] Diego: Ok diving in: latency numbers depend a lot on model shape and quantization. If you quantize some models you get 2-3x throughput improvements with small perf accuracy tradeoffs. For GPU types, Ampere instances vs Ada-series differ on FP16 kernels — we choose kernels at runtime.
[05:36] Jae: Do you do INT8 in the runtime? We have models we can quantize offline but worried about accuracy drift.
[05:44] Diego: We support INT8 and mixed quantization paths; appraisal tests are needed. The runtime has quantization-friendly execution to avoid KV cache corruption.
[05:53] Omar: On autoscaling — how fast can you scale GPUs up? Bursting is key for our sales use-case.
[06:00] Diego: Autoscaling is policy-driven; warm pools reduce spin-up time. For dedicated pools we suggest warm standby nodes to handle bursts. Cold spin up depends on infra (minutes), warm pools give sub-minute.
[06:12] Ruth: If we want to resell, do we manage billing surface or you do white-label billing?
[06:18] Maya: We can do partner invoicing, or you can resell under your contract. We also support marketplace billing integrations.
[06:26] Jae: Do you capture prompt telemetry for debugging? We have privacy constraints and need opt-outs for certain customer datasets.
[06:34] Diego: Telemetry is configurable — you can opt to redact prompts, and we support strict data retention policies. For regulated customers we recommend Private with E2E encryption and customer KMS.
[06:47] Omar: Let's talk network topologies. VPC peering vs PrivateLink? Which do you use typically?
[06:53] Diego: Both are supported; VPC peering is simple for same-cloud, PrivateLink (or interconnect) useful across accounts/regions. For cross-cloud we do VPN/DirectConnect setups.
[07:05] Ruth: Cool. Any reference partner case studies for this reseller + private mix?
[07:11] Maya: We'll include two anonymized case studies in the partner deck — one reseller hybrid, one on-prem private deployment for regulated customer.

[07:20] [Short pause, folks reviewing shared screen]

[07:25] Samir: A few clarifying Qs for the benchmark: 1) can you share a script template for load gen? 2) do you want raw traces or only aggregated metrics?
[07:34] Diego: We'll provide a load script (wrk-style) and prefer both traces and aggregates. Traces help triage p95 spikes.
[07:41] Jae: How do you deal with model fallbacks? If a larger model suffers latency we may want automatic fallback to a smaller variant.
[07:48] Diego: We have routing policies supporting fallback chains — route to cheaper/smaller variants on late tails or capacity constraints. It is policy-driven and configurable per-route.

[07:58] Ruth: Let's cover the commercial outline briefly — what's a typical contract for a pilot?
[08:03] Maya: Typically a 3-month pilot with reserved baseline and overage. We'll propose a pilot SOW with committed GPUs, a price per-hour for reserved units, and a surge overage rate. We'll include partner margin options.
[08:15] Omar: What SLAs do you commit to in pilots?
[08:18] Maya: For pilots we commit to availability SLAs for dedicated pools in the SOW and operational support hours. Production Dedicated has full SLAs.

[08:27] Diego: Quick note on observability: our tracing attaches request IDs that you can ingest into your logging; we also expose per-route cost meters so you can show customers exact cost per inference.
[08:38] Jae: We'll definitely want that.

[08:44] Ruth: Any integration work from our side for the reseller flow? We have a billing system that expects line-itemized usage.
[08:51] Maya: We can push line-item usage via S3 exports, or via API. We'll map to your billing schema in the partner onboarding.

[09:00] Samir: To summarize technical asks for the benchmark: sample prompts, sequence length distribution, QPS patterns (steady vs burst), and representative models. PixelWorkz to provide those. Redwood to produce test plan and run initial benchmark on staging.

[09:15] Ruth: Sounds good — high level questions from my side answered. One more: how long to get a basic dedicated pool turned up for a pilot?
[09:23] Diego: If using hosted capacity we can spin a dedicated pool in 24-48 hours; if it's private VPC there's a bit more network config, usually 3-7 days depending on approvals.

[09:34] Omar: Are there any specific dependencies for private deployments? Firewall ports, repo access?
[09:40] Diego: We'll send a network checklist — egress, certs, KMS endpoints, and IAM roles required. Also we'll include an on-prem install matrix if you go that route.

[09:53] Ruth: Okay, let's capture next steps then.
[09:57] Maya: I'll recap: Maya sends partner deck and SOW template by Aug 9, Diego sends benchmark test plan and load script by Aug 12, Jae shares workload snapshots and model artifacts (where license permits) by Aug 11, and we schedule POC kickoff week of Aug 19.
[10:14] Ruth: Perfect. We'll also pull in our legal and billing folks once we get the SOW.

[10:22] Omar: One minor point — latency budgets for three enterprise customers are p95 < 150ms for certain image endpoints. Can you hit that with a 34B model?
[10:32] Diego: That will be tough with larger models; likely solution is a smaller distilled variant or hardware acceleration (Ada or H100 depending). The benchmark will show which combo meets the p95.
[10:44] Jae: Do you offer custom kernel work to squeeze latency?
[10:47] Diego: We do some low-level kernel selection and model compilation, but custom kernel engineering is scoped case-by-case and may be part of professional services.

[10:56] Ruth: Any blockers remaining from legal compliance? We must ensure covered datacenter regions for EU customers.
[11:02] Maya: We have regional deployments in EU currently, and we can restrict data residency in Private deployments. We'll mark the regions in the security docs.

[11:12] Samir: Final quick note on success criteria for pilot: measurable p50/p95 latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, and successful reseller billing integration. If those are green we move to full pipeline.
[11:25] Ruth: Sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone.

[11:28] Maya: Great — we'll send the materials. Any final quick questions?
[11:31] Omar: None here.
[11:33] Lena: Nope, thanks.

[11:35] Maya: Ok thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the deck and SOW template.

[11:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional words may be mis-recognized (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" vs Redwood Dedicated, "KV cash" instead of KV cache). Shared artifacts: partner-deck.pdf (link shared in chat), benchmark-template.xlsx (link).
